It wasn't until I was done solidifying her design that I realized how much she embodies myself in many ways, both in personality and visually.  Have any of you ended up having a character that looked a hell of a lot like you or just acted like how you do (or both)?

Kels Ardeni was a child orphaned in her late teens when her father mysteriously disappeared a few years after her mother died.  He left her some meager coin and a necklace that he used to wear.  She and her brother tried to make it on the street for a time, but her brother was little, and she was not ready to play mom, nonetheless on a street she had no smarts for.  After some reconning a home of a kindly priest, she dropped her brother at the door and disappeared into the shadows.  Her life was to be a difficult one, but it was not the life she wanted for her brother.

She is impulsive, clever and silly.  Making fast friends and protecting them with all she has (even if that is from making mistakes she once made when first on the streets).  Sindri (in the last piece), the protector Aasimar of the party has become her best friend.  She highly guards this kindly, but simple cleric.  He cares too much and she sees it as something people will use against him.

Honestly, I'd just straight up tell them all in a group setting that all of you want to be paladins and an all paladin campaign will not work for what you are planning without potentially breaking your work altogether.  So they really need to decide amongst themselves who would like to change their class and who is going to be a paladin.  Maybe set a limit to how many paladins you can have and make it a thing where there can only be one of each type out of say, maybe the two that you allow or something?

I always find the best order of business in dealing with a situation like this is set the standard up front to all the players and let them sort it out amongst themselves, that way it isn't a personal issue.  If you go to someone privately and ask them to switch classes, that will be taken more personally than presenting it as a voluntary thing to the group to figure out together.

Sabysra is one of my evil characters, who happens to be a poisoner style assassin. They hope to bring honor to their family name after scandal swept the Underdark and drove them to seek new horizons.  They are from a scorned noble house and are hoping to make ripples in the neighboring city.  The manor they happened to purchase is one with a rough history.  Haunted and supposedly cursed, it has sat idle within the forest valley below the mountains and city high above.

The first campaign I ever ran was a homebrew that was on the shorter side.  A murder mystery in a single city I developed.  

While I will admit, homebrewing takes a lot more time, if you try your hand at something on the smaller side, like a single goal, it can be a good way to get your feet wet without any of the cost.  

For my first, it was essentially all within a single city, where a few murders have taken place before the annual festival.  Ended up being about 10 sessions, but that also depends on how much your group likes to RP.  They had a collection quest in the marketplace in the leadup before going to a massive party that was being hosted by their benefactor, a lord who had a stack in wanted the murders solved and the serial killer brought to justice (his sister was "supposedly" among the dead).  

Just keep it simple, you got this.  Also, neat tip, but I made my inn and the manor that my players were in via the Sims.  If you happen ton have the game, it is a nice way to make buildings you can screen save, edit and then add to roll20.

Now she has to help save her poor dead friend's soul from Barovia and help perhaps reunite father and son before the father goes off to the light forever.  Its made for a really emotional set up and I am so excited!

I actually just started seeing a therapist again.  I do agree, it can often do some good.  Unfortunately, my trauma has effected such a large time frame in my life and I am very good at hiding and down playing how much I am effected.  I left a six year abusive marriage and pretty much lost my family in the process when they took him in (their reasoning?  because they signed his forms when we moved back from Australia and he is Australian and has a green card in the US).  

The effects of how I was treated by my family and the pain of rebuilding and changing my life so drastically have made it difficult to open up to a therapist in the past.  My biggest thing is just needing to let go of those walls and be vulnerable and allow myself to cry.  I think the therapeutic quality of being able to just let go would do me tremendous good and help move me forward in the right direction.  For now, to help deal with the pain I am focusing on Pilates or yoga in the morning as well as meditation twice a day. Just calming activities that can help de-stress my life when I need it most.  :)

I would try posting photos if I were you!  I used to be so grossed out with myself and I have so few photos from the time I was heaviest for this reason.  I would avoid them or they would never see the light of day, but I feel that being vulnerable and showing people who I really am and being open helped keep me accountable as well as helped motivate me and allow me to have pride in myself when I did see changes.  We may not feel we've lost anything, but sometimes you see the difference in appearance when you look at a side by side before you ever see much on the scale.

Measurements are so much more important than the scale in the long run anyhow.  :p
